As a shadow, I follow my person everywhere they go. I start the day when they wake up, stretching across the floor as the morning light peeks through the curtains. They get out of bed, and I mimic their movements, rising and falling with each step.

In the bathroom, I watch as they brush their teeth and get ready. The mirror reflects both of us, but only they can see themselves. I'm just a dark outline, always present but often unnoticed.

At breakfast, I sit beside them, casting a faint shadow on the table. The sunlight changes as the day progresses, making me longer or shorter. When they walk outside, I stretch out on the pavement, keeping pace with their strides.

In the office, I lurk under their desk or climb the walls when they move around. During meetings, I'm a silent companion, never speaking but always there. When they laugh, I don't move, but when they frown, I remain still, just a shape.

Lunchtime brings a walk in the park. The trees cast their own shadows, and I blend in, sometimes disappearing when the light is just right. But I'm always there, waiting for them to step back into the sun.
